patterns: what are the rounds in placement
what are the steps for getting a job through campus
responses: A typical campus drive has: 1) Pre-placement talk, 2) Online aptitude/coding test, 3) Group discussion (some companies), 4) Technical interview, 5) HR interview, 6) Offer letter. Each company may skip or add a round.

patterns: can i sit for amazon with 7 cgpa

responses: Most companies ask for 60% or 6.0+ CGPA throughout (10th, 12th, graduation) and no active backlogs. Use the 'Eligibility' tab to check company-wise criteria with your own marks.

patterns: name some companies for campus drive

responses: Common recruiters include TCS, Infosys, Wipro, Cognizant, Accenture, Capgemini, Zoho, Amazon and Microsoft. Check the 'Eligibility' tab for sample criteria of each.

patterns: how much salary do freshers get
responses: Service companies typically offer 3.5-7 LPA to freshers, while product companies and top startups offer 10-45+ LPA depending on role and performance. Exact packages vary each year.

patterns: how to make a good resume

how long should a resume be
how to write a resume for placement
responses: Keep it to 1 page. Include: contact info, education, skills, 2-3 projects (with tech stack and results), internships, certifications. Use action verbs and numbers (e.g., 'reduced load time by 30%'). Try the 'Resume Check' tab for an instant score.

patterns: what questions are asked in interview

how to perform well in interview
how to prepare for technical interview
how to be confident in interview
what should i do in an interview
responses: Revise core subjects (DSA, DBMS, OS, OOP, CN), be ready to explain every project line on your resume, practise 'Tell me about yourself' in 60 seconds, think aloud while solving problems, and ask a good question at the end.

patterns: how to prepare for aptitude test
how to solve quant problems fast
what is asked in aptitude test
responses: Focus on percentages, profit & loss, time-speed-distance, time & work, number series, blood relations, and verbal (synonyms, grammar). Practise daily with timers. Try the 'Mock Quiz' tab!

patterns: how to prepare for coding round

how to prepare coding for placement
how to learn data structures and algorithms
how to practice programming for interviews
responses: Pick one language (C++/Java/Python). Master arrays, strings, linked lists, stacks, queues, trees, graphs, recursion and DP. Solve 150-300 problems on LeetCode/GeeksforGeeks, and practise writing code without an IDE.

patterns: how to do well in group discussion
how to speak in group discussion
responses: In a GD: listen first, start with a short fact or definition, speak clearly with 2-3 points, never interrupt rudely, support others' points, and summarise at the end if possible.

patterns: how to get internship as a fresher
responses: Internships add real experience and often lead to pre-placement offers. Look at Internshala, LinkedIn, company career pages, and your college TPO cell. Even virtual internships and open-source contributions help your resume.

patterns: what documents to carry for interview
list of documents for campus drive
what to bring on interview day
responses: Carry: updated resume (3-4 copies), photo ID (Aadhaar/college ID), 10th, 12th and all semester mark sheets, degree/provisional certificate, passport photos, and certificates for achievements/internships.

patterns: what should i wear to campus drive
what dress should i wear for placement
responses: Wear formals: light shirt, dark trousers, formal shoes (men) or formal kurta/shirt-trousers/saree (women). Keep it clean, ironed and simple. Neat grooming and a confident smile matter.

patterns: how to apply for campus drive
how do i enroll in placement cell
how to sign up for placement
how do i register for campus drive
responses: Register with your college Training & Placement Office (TPO) portal, upload your resume and marksheets, and then apply to each company drive before its deadline. Watch your college email for notifications.

patterns: what should i learn for placement

what skills should i learn to get placed
responses: In demand: DSA + one language, SQL, web basics (HTML/CSS/JS, React), Python, cloud basics (AWS/Azure), Git, plus communication and teamwork. For data roles add statistics, pandas and ML basics.

patterns: should i do mtech or job
should i go for higher studies
responses: If you want research, specialised roles or a switch of domain, go for higher studies (GATE/GRE/CAT). If you want early experience and income, take the job - you can still pursue part-time or sponsored higher studies later.
